Done. The task passed on the first and only execution.

**What the script does** (`out/T3/solution.py`):
- Loads the 244-tensor float16 checkpoint and iterates in input order.
- Drops the 48 buffers matched by an anchored regex on the three buffer names.
- Casts the 64 projection matrices, matched by an anchored regex on the four exact names, to bfloat16.
- Upcasts every remaining tensor to float32.
- Runs the required checks before writing: 64 bfloat16 tensors, layer-0 query_key_value is bfloat16, embed_in is float32, 196 output tensors, plus match-count and key-set checks.
- Shards greedily under the 256 MiB budget, placing each oversized embedding matrix alone, and writes an HF-style index with a weight map.
- Reloads all shards and verifies dtypes, shapes and bit-exact values against the in-memory result.

**Output** in `out/T3/`:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Shards | 9 |
| Tensors | 196 |
| Largest shard data | 260,317,184 bytes (under budget) |
| Embedding shards | 412,090,368 bytes each, one tensor alone |

The self-report is at `out/T3/REPORT.md`. It notes two unspecified points: shard file naming and index metadata followed the HuggingFace convention, and sharding used input tensor order rather than sorted order.
